body:
Hi @ncw. I'm the maintainer of the go-smb2 fork at github.com/cloudsoda/go-smb2. I've fixed this issue in a local branch, and will be bringing it into `main` later today or tomorrow.

In the interest of making the 'right' way of using the library the only of using the library, I want to replace the existing `Dial(net.Conn)` and `DialContext(context.Context, net.Conn)` methods with a single `Dial(ctx context.Context, addr string)`. The new method will handle the tcp connection creation. Would removing the ability to provide a `net.Conn` be a problem for rclone?

@arashpayan 
> I'm the maintainer of the go-smb2 fork at github.com/cloudsoda/go-smb2. I've fixed this issue in a local branch, and will be bringing it into `main` later today or tomorrow.

Great!

> In the interest of making the 'right' way of using the library the only of using the library, I want to replace the existing `Dial(net.Conn)` and `DialContext(context.Context, net.Conn)` methods with a single `Dial(ctx context.Context, addr string)`. The new method will handle the tcp connection creation. Would removing the ability to provide a `net.Conn` be a problem for rclone?

Yes... Rclone has its own Dialer (created with `fshttp.NewDialer`) which does all sorts of great stuff (like set QoS, do rate limiting etc). It wouldn't be the end of the world to lose this but it would be nice to keep it.

You could fix this by allowing a config parameter for the user to supply their own `DialContext` in `smb2.Dialer`

    DialContext(ctx context.Context, network, address string) (net.Conn, error)

Here is the code in rclone so you can take a look

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/668711e43213bc9464c0b25c88621cd987898f08/backend/smb/connpool.go#L16-L19

PS as far as rclone goes, please feel free to break the API! As long as it fails to compile I don't care. If you break the API and it still compiles then I probably won't notice!
Interesting. Those look like worthwhile settings in `fshttp`. I'll make sure to provide a way for rclone to keep leveraging that.

issue.title: Share pathname should use hostname when available in TREE_CONNECT requests

repository.name: go-smb2
repository.description: Client implementation of the SMB 2 & 3 protocols

issue.body:
When performing a `TREE_CONNECT` request servers sometimes vary their response based on the server component of the share path (e.g. `\\server\share`). The library just passes the resolved IP address from the `net.Conn` that was passed to it, but that causes problems for users. In particular, missing shares and incorrect file listings. Some public examples of this problem:

https://github.com/hirochachacha/go-smb2/issues/40
https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/6672
and possibly this: https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/6515

We need to include the server hostname in the share path sent with the `TREE_CONNECT` request to avoid these problems.

Per consultation with @ncw (https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/6672#issuecomment-1823260480), we'll still allow the user to provide their own `net.Conn` if they like.

body: :wave: @halms. @ncw already switched rclone over to using github.com/cloudsoda/go-smb2 a few days ago. I think you just need to wait for a release now. :slightly_smiling_face:

Yes, but it's currently on a [previous version](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/96f8b7c827261200dad7d7d786f6778cb87e0992/go.mod#L23), and for the latest, `connpool.go` needs a small change.
https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/96f8b7c827261200dad7d7d786f6778cb87e0992/backend/smb/connpool.go#L43
```diff
-	session, err := d.DialContext(ctx, tconn)
+	session, err := d.DialConn(ctx, tconn, addr)
```

Ah, yes. Then please open up a PR. That would be great.

BTW, I tried reproducing the problem on a FSx Windows File Server but I couldn't reproduce it. Do you know what setting(s) in particular was causing the server to require this fix?

issue.title: smb: fix shares not listed by updating go-smb2

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?
Before this change the IP address of the server was used in the SMB connect request (see CloudSoda/go-smb2#18).
Depending on the server configuration this could lead to servers responding differently, e.g., `\\hostname\share` is available, but `\\ip\share` is not.

The updated library now can pass the hostname instead.
The signature of the `Dial*` methods was changed by the library and `connpool.go` updated accordingly.

Fixes rclone#6672

#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?
Issue: rclone#6672
Underlying issue: CloudSoda/go-smb2#18

body:
[PR](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/pull/7465) opened.

I don't know what it exactly is (I don't have any insight how this FSx was setup, I'm just a consumer in that regard).
From what I see, it is a drive joined to an AD with an internal domain name `amznfsx···.xxx.local` in a private network.

Overall it just is as described here / in [your issue](https://github.com/CloudSoda/go-smb2/issues/18):
When the IP address is used in the server part of the share the the share is not available, when the correct hostname is used, then it works.

I've merged this to master now which means it will be in [the latest beta](https://beta.rclone.org/) in 15-30 minutes and released in v1.66 - I'll probably release it in v1.64.1 also.

Thank you @halms  and @arashpayan
